instruction: I'm planning a trip to Hong Kong and have compiled a list of restaurants I'd love to visit. Could you please help me by searching for these restaurants on Google Maps and filling in their basic information? I need you to find and enter the address, website, and phone number for each restaurant listed in my text file into the corresponding Excel spreadsheet. Thank you!

metadata.explanation: This variation checks that all 5 restaurant names from restaurants.txt are correctly filled into the Excel file (rows 2-6, column A). The evaluator extracts the names and verifies all expected names are present with partial credit (0.2 per restaurant).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.2 per restaurant name correctly filled (5 total)

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete coverage: The instruction requires filling in THREE types of information (address, website, phone number) for each restaurant, but the evaluator ONLY checks that restaurant names are present in column A

Wrong verification target: The evaluator verifies restaurant names exist, but the core task is to LOOK UP and FILL IN contact information (address/website/phone) from Google Maps. Checking names doesn't verify the actual task completion

Missing data extraction: The getter only extracts names from column A (cells A2:A6) but doesn't check if columns B, C, D (or other columns) contain the required address, website, and phone number data

Semantic mismatch: The instruction implies restaurant names should come from restaurants.txt (already known), while the actual work is searching Google Maps and populating contact details. The evaluator doesn't verify this core requirement at all
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Expand the getter to extract not just names, but also address, website, and phone number from appropriate columns (e.g., columns B, C, D)
Update the metric to verify all three required fields (address, website, phone) are filled for each restaurant, not just the name

Consider using a more comprehensive comparison: for each of the 5 restaurants, check that all 3 contact fields are non-empty and potentially valid (e.g., phone numbers have digits, websites have URLs, addresses are non-empty strings)

Adjust partial credit logic: instead of 0.2 per name, award credit based on complete information per restaurant (e.g., 0.2 per restaurant × (fields_filled/3), so a restaurant with name+address but no phone gets 0.2×2/3=0.133)
